newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest shares end mixed in bearish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest shares end mixed in bearish sentiment.

text.p: Bucharest share prices ended mixed on Thursday with buying interest low among investors who adopted a wait-and-see attitude.
Traders said the bearish mood recorded in recent days was likely to continue.

"Most investors say the present prices are too high and wait now for them to go lower. Their attitude was also encouraged by the fact that most prices went down in recent days under selling pressure," one said.

Some investors who used to trade heavily in first-tier listings had tentatively switched to second-tier stocks but the move had little impact as they had been so far reluctant to invest large amounts, brokers said.
Two independent market indices, the VAB and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, went down from the Wednesday session, sliding 2.5 and 2.75 percent respectively.
Prices of 18 stocks inched up, 20 went down and eight were flat. Two stocks stayed suspended and one had no trade.
"There is little action at the bourse now as both investors and brokers are on summer holidays," a broker said.
Turnover slipped to 8.68 billion lei from 10.47 billion previously and volume edged down to 2.38 million shares from 2.41 million in the previous session.
First-tier listings took around 77 percent from overall turnover with chemical plant Oltchim, which closed flat at 4,200, being the most active stock.

Among first-tier stocks, fertiliser maker Azomures also closed flat at 3,500 while dye maker Policolor gained 100 lei to close at 6,500 and Sofert SOFE.BX fertiliser maker closed 1,500 lei firmer at 32,000.
On the second tier, stocks traded mixed and lost steam under selling pressure.
